App is quirky. Content is good.. The UI of the app is quirky and takes some time to figure out. For example, to exit a course, there is no standard iOS back button at the top left (on iPad), but you have to first tap the video player once to show its hidden controls and then tap x. The UI quirkiness is compounded by bugs like the full screen video player sometimes crashing if you try to scrub video. The next video does not always autoplay. Sometimes it does and sometimes it doesn’t. There is no obvious setting for enabling/disabling autoplay. Sometimes you can scroll the tablature viewer up/down, and sometimes you can’t. At one point, I somehow accidentally pinched to zoom the entire app interface and all the navigation controls were zoomed off screen. I could not figure out how to zoom back out and had to just quit the app. Things often don’t work like you’d expect them to or work reliably.

Good content, but the app UI can make it frustrating to use. It does get better if you take the time to learn the app’s several UI oddities that are not standard for iOS and can tolerate occasional bugs.

If, for instance, there is a course with 4 lessons - each has a video, tab under the video and the ability to launch into GP - often the tab related to the video is really for another video. So you are watching lesson 3, but the tab for 2 or 4 shows. I try clicking above and below to get to the proper tab to view, to no avail.

Stoping in the middle of a lesson then coming back often results in the video not being playable, coupled with the wrong tab.

Sometimes the ability to return to the main screen/dashboard doesn’t work.

This happens on courses I purchased in order to have them on my iPad via download. 

The only way to resolve this is to quit and relaunch, which can become a bit tedious depending on how often the bug shows up.

The lessons are not only top-quality but really fun and engaging. They really focus on musicality aside from being very specific on technical skills. They zoom in on the specific “feeling” behind a given technique and what it communicates and make learning much easier. I am also impressed by the selection of themes for each course. For instance, Sue Foley’s Trail Blazers course, which focuses on six legendary female guitarrists. Sophie Lloyd’s Bulletproof Rock Guitar course, too. It really feels like the curators for the courses want everyone to feel
included. I also really like that we can purchase individual courses to own forever instead of having to get the monthly membership, even though the latter is also a great option. I couldn’t be happier with the platform and will keep coming back for more courses!

App Does Not Live Up to the TrueFire and Jamplay Content. This review is just for the TrueFire app. I am a long time Jamplay subscriber, and was recently shunted into the TrueFire ecosystem (I had put the guitar down for a while and didn’t realize that Jamplayed and moved all their contact over to TrueFire. The Jamplay app doesn’t work anymore).

There is obviously a lot more content now with the two platforms combined. And going through the website, TruFire does seem to be pretty well thought out and put together but the app really kind of stinks. The Jamplay app wasn’t fantastic, but it was definitely better than the TrueFire app.

There are many areas for possible improvement, but I will focus on the three I find the most important:

1)The Landing zones for the player controls seem to be seriously messed up. The player rarely responds in the way that I intended and I find myself tapping on the screen over and over again trying to get to the spot in the video where I want to be, the scrub bar is almost as bad as the buttons. Perhaps they’re all just too small.

2)The lesson tree and progress indicators are completely disconnected from your viewing activity in the app. You have two scroll up and down the lesson free to find the place where you left off. And you have to manually update your lesson progress. This is just unnecessarily frustrating.

3)It seems like a lot of the notes and comments from jim play have been left behind. It looks like TruFire prefers to use discord for dialogue (which is another issue) but all the notes and comments from the years I’ve been using Jamplay seem to be lost.

It’s a decent app and I don’t think there’s a better option available currently, but it seems like a step backward, and there’s a lot of room for improvement.

Apps and web interface inconsistent. I have been on and off Truefire for years. I am an all access member now. It is actually a good deal as compared to other options. The apps can be frustrating though. I use the iOS app, the browser interface, and sometimes the android app on a chromebook. You cannot access everything on each of these, and they work very differently. One example, you can get the song lessons on the web but not on the android app. Another: you can create folders on one of these (cant remember which) but cant access them on another. How you do things or find things is very different. The features are very different. Often i am trying to do something or find something and i have to switch from the app to the browser or vice versa. This has been the case with Truefire for years and is the one thing that always drives me to cancel. As a former multiple time startup software company CEO, this is kind of an unforgivable sin. You can have temporary or well documented inconsistencies, but to go on like this for years is really bad. ALL THE FUNCTIONALITY SHOULD BE IN THE APP. PERIOD. 

Second, you have what I can only describe as scope creep. You now have playlists, favorites and folders. You have courses, learning paths, curated collections, etc. It is confusing. It feels like what happens when the creative side says ac this, add that, and the developers have to keep bolting stiff on. This is a classic product management failure. 

The other thing that frustrates me is kind of not fixable, which is that the courses are very different over time. The newer lessons have better tools than the older ones. The older ones, you tend to get a video and a PDF. Also, each teacher kind of does things however they want so the styles are wildly different, and its hard to know what “level” you are going to get. Some are super basic and some are nuclear physics.
